_comment: Registration for the liveness judgement of scripts/flow-worktree-claim.sh (issue #1726).
WHY IT NEEDS COMMITTED CASES (ADR 0008): the helper's verdict decides whether a
second session may take a worktree and whether worktree-remove.sh may delete it,
and neither caller re-derives it. Until #1726 the script had tests and no
TWO BAD CASES, the two ways 'some process has this number' is not 'the owner is
alive': the pid was recycled (#1032), and the owner exited but was never reaped
(#1605). Each read `held`, which left --steal - the override for a genuinely
live owner - as the only way to clean up after a dead one.
detect_signal: ^FLOW_CLAIM_CONTROL: finding - the claim's owner is gone
limits: Covers the CHECK verdict for a same-host claim whose owner pid exists: recycled, zombie, alive. It does not cover a Codex session's owner pid, a live process whose main thread exited, the age bound for an unverifiable claim, another host, the claim and release verbs or their mutex, or any usage error - those are pinned by tests/test_flow_worktree_claim.py, tests/test_flow_worktree_claim_owner.py and tests/test_merge_tail_refusals.py. The process table is a fixture, so nothing here depends on a real process.

cases.name: bad-owner-pid-recycled
cases.why: The pid exists but started at a different instant than the claim recorded: another process wearing a recycled number. If it scores GOOD the claim is held forever by a session that is gone.

cases.name: bad-owner-is-a-zombie
cases.why: The owner exited and was never reaped: pid and start time still match, and it can never touch the worktree again. If it scores GOOD, kill -0 succeeding is being read as alive.

cases.name: good-owner-alive
cases.why: The owning process is running and is the one that claimed. Separates a working check from one wedged at stale, which would hand a live session's worktree to the next caller.

cases.name: good-no-claim
cases.why: An unclaimed worktree reads free, not stale.

anchors.why: HISTORICAL: the helper at the last commit before #1032, where liveness was kill -0 alone. It calls both the recycled and the zombie owner held. The commit is on main's history, so --verify-provenance can compare it.
